cards.title: Deleting a merged branch
cards.body: Once a branch is merged, `git branch -d <name>` deletes it. Its commits stay safe in `main`.
cards.code:
git init
touch a.txt
git add .
git commit -m "Start"
git switch -c extra
touch b.txt
git add .
git commit -m "Add b"
git switch main
git merge extra
git branch -d extra
git branch

cards.title: Git protects unmerged work
cards.body: `-d` refuses to delete a branch whose commits aren't merged yet, so you can't lose work by accident.

cards.title: Spot the bug
cards.body: Git refuses to delete `extra`. Tap the line that runs too early.
cards.code:
git init
touch a.txt
git add .
git commit -m "Start"
git switch -c extra
touch b.txt
git add .
git commit -m "Add b"
git switch main
git branch -d extra

bug.fix: `extra` is not merged yet, so `-d` protects its work. Run `git merge extra` first, then delete the branch.

check.question: `git branch -d footer` says the branch is "not fully merged". What does that mean?
options: Its commits are not in your current branch yet
check.explanation: Deleting it now would lose those commits, so Git stops you.

exercise.prompt: `footer` is already merged into `main`. Delete the `footer` branch.
